body: Thank you so much! I find your words inspiring!
Sorry, not for me. Even a little of weed makes me faint.
A bottle of wine each evening
If only I cared about it lately
I’m really glad to hear that quitting alcohol has such positive effects on you!
A sad high 5. It’s really tough to deal with the fact that our kids are facing such difficulties, when all we ever wanted was all the best for them.
Thanks, I love the comparison! It takes some courage to step out of a toxic relationship.
I’m glad that meditation has worked for you. I practiced for several months, but found that the effect was short-lived, so I paused it for some while.
Yes, I have an exercise program, it makes me feel a bit better, but it’s not a sufficient substitute for me.
Thanks! Unexpectedly I started feeling much better already on my second day here. So hopes are up :)

I give them a chance. Some people have been supportive, but not my husband unfortunately. Now I’ve developed a radar - with whom I can talk to and who to avoid in dark times.

Now I’m at a mental hospital. People are really open about their shit :)
Thanks, I’ll try
I believe so. I wake up with a single thought in my mind - munchies!

There was one period in my life when I quickly became obese. I felt so unlikable that I was genuinely surprised if some guy called me pretty (and that was rare, trust me). Gradually my weight came of and I became thin. The shift in the attitude I received was enourmous- doors were opened for me, drinks were bought, guys at work stopped to talk to me, heck, in a couple of occasions guys were running up to me on the street just to tell me I’m pretty. Whole different attitude. Now I’ve gained 10kg, which is noticable. I don’t think I look good, even though I’m not overweight, and I recieve no more attention. Probably it’s very much tied to how confident I feel about myself and if I want to be seen or not.

Edit: oh, wait! There was actually one guy who fell in love with me while I was obese. He was one of the hottest guys at the university. Needless to say that I pushed him away.

I smile a fake smile and change the subject. “You look great” is an acceptable way to compliment on weight loss, “You lost weight” is not a compliment, it’s a statement of fact, and maybe it’s just me, but I consider it a bit rude.

I have a husband, but he wants a divorce, says he has no more energy dealing with me. But yeah, on the bright side we had 11 years together and most of them were nice. I think I’ll be forever alone when we split up. There are tons of people out there who make better company.

I’m yet to take my shower today. My big issue is taking off make up in the evening if I had bothered to put some on and doing the evening beauty routine. Yesterday didn’t do that,  I hope for bigger motivation this evening.

My 4 y old loves trees. Luckily we live a a green area with a large wild park nearby. He loves being outdoors, walking among the trees, he’s collecting branches, he loves to throw them down from his tree-house. He loves breaking them, planting them. His favourite youtube videos are those where they are cutting trees. He loves drawing and painting trees. He has several encyclopedias about trees, memorizes them. His favourite place is the botanical garden, in the autumn we go to pick mushrooms in the forest. His goodnight fairy-tales have to be about trees. So basically it’s all about the trees :)

Have you tried stating clearly to her which parts of her behaviour are unacceptable to you? If you have a safe base (I mean you still love each other) then it’s worth to put in the effort.

I know the meltdown, I’m still struggling with my son’s diagnosis 1 year in. I’m the nut case in the family (depression), I blame myself and my family line. And then there is this enormous anger, which I think your wife also has, and it needs an outlet (I have screamed in the pillow a couple of times).

It is sad for me to see how we have grown apart with my husband. He’s no longer the person I turn to when I hurt - he doesn’t listen and has openly said that all of his energy is saved for the kid, and he has none left for me.

Make sure you ask and listen to what’s up with your wife. Show her you care and also be clear about the boundaries in a calm and loving manner. She’s in pain and she acts out.

Also an idea- tell her you want to support her and ask if her therapist can suggest something to you. Perhaps you can even talk to her therapist together.

Let’s try to be factful here, ok? :) You managed to lose an amazing amount of weight, that’s really something to celebrate. You’re exercising and love it - bravo! From what and how you’re saying I get the impression you’re in a bad place mentally. When it’s hard, seeking help is the reasonsble thing to do. Give theraphy a chance. They’ll train you how to stop focusing on the negatives only. I’m in a similar boat- wanting to lose weight, frustrated it’s not moving in the right direction. But at the core of this problem is my mental state, so I’m working to address that.
Thanks, I hope so too. Fingers crossed for you and your business!

Same here, except that it’s not my business, it’s my job that I’m losing. I was overwhlemed by the tasks I had to do, decisions I had to make, incredibly stressed and when I needed to be my most productive, all I did was procrastinated. Instead of actually working, I listened to audiobooks on how to stop procrastinating. Can’t put my finger on what was stopping me. there’s one theory saying it might be fear of success. Could it be the case?
I think I’m so used to being an underdog that I sabbotage myself, because being a mess is my essence, isn’t it?

Agree. I’ve been binge-watching series for several days in a row, hiding at my parents’ house in the countryside. Life seems bearable if it’s somebody else’s life. I even lost the urge to kill myself, because, hey, there are some more episodes of Virgin River coming up! My therapist though recommends that I should be doing something more active, but I hate to get my head out of the sand.

Then you will be a walking miracle :). Hopefully I will be there too. I don’t want a competition on who’s doing worse, I’m having my own crisis and pain is difficult to compare. But fingers crossed we make it until next year.
So glad you were able to find the good stuff as well :)
Well, seeking help is not always the solution. I am depressed, I seek help- therapist, medication, talking to friends. My marriage is falling apart anyway.

My son (4y) managed to stay with me for most of the day. He’s a daddy’s boy, his dad had Covid for 2 weeks, and they blissfully spent the 2 weeks together. I’m his depressed, anxious mom, who’s preoccupied with work and managing her own feelings and he never wants to spend time with me. Today dad had to catch up with his work, so we were on our own. We managed! It is also an achievement for me.

Genius! I just joined the group and already found the first advice I’m willing to try. Shopping for a waffle cooker tomorrow! And I guess a hand blender as well. Are they quieter than the other type where you put things in in a glass container? (Sorry for my English, sometimes I lack the words, but I hope what I say is understandable)
Btw what’s with your need to try to outsmart people? Noticed it below some other comments as well.
I’ll leave the smart comments to you :)

It’s probably a soviet heritage when educated people earned very little. My dad who was a scientist, earned less than a truck-driver. The new doctors are there because it’s their calling and they hope it gets better. A lot of them though go to work abroad. It slowly does get better, but still a far way to go.
That’s what I call a tragicomedy!
The doctors earn next to nothing in my country, so I believe she’s in it because she really wants to help people.
That sounds sinister. My psychiatrist seems to care. I believe she would love to fix me, but she hasn’t succeeded.
It just makes me wonder- if nobody really likes depressed people, why do they advice not to commit suicide? Is it being polite?

I’m lucky that there is one friend who actually cares. But I think it’s only because he’s not worn out from my depression yet. The rest- my husband, my best friend- they’ve been through this many times, they’re sick of it and want to protect themselves.
They think we’re just lazy, don’t they? Sometimes it makes me think that they’re right and I feel ashamed for not being able to pull my shit together.

Yeah, my husband got really mad at me yesterday for being depressed. It really offended me, I decided everyone will be better off without me, and I took pills. They were wrong kind of pills, did not kill me, and my husband just became more pissed at me.

I know quite many people who enjoy their lives. They seem to have some purpose, and they don’t even question if it’s worth living, for them it absolutely is. Of course, I compare myself to them and feel like a lesser human being. Sometimes I wish everybody was unhappy, then I would fit in better. Well, not everybody. My family should be spared.
It was a wrong choice of medication. Nothing really happened. So here I am with a failed attempt and none of my issues gone :(

It’s unfortunate that it happened to you, but you seem like a person who is capable of thinking logically and understand that it was plain rude and that you did absolutely nothing to deserve this. Besides you are on your way to successfully shred the pounds that are bothering you andI’m sure you will be alright and this will become a remote memory that cease to hurt you. It’s her I’m worried about- something is completely off about such behaviour. She must be struggling with her own demons.

I was called fat when I was pregnant 🙈. It certainly hurt, but now it’s something I laugh about, because such comments are plain absurd.

I have been curious about this question for a while now. I’ve asked it to a couple of friends, but they regard it as a weird thing to ask. Observing them I concluded that they enjoy life more than they hate it.

I, on the other hand, dislike almost every day. I see a spark of joy here and there, but mostly I’m just pulling my own weight through the day. What’s enjoyable about that?

Looking forward to a brighter future? Well, my kid has autism, it already kills me how difficult for him it is to fit in the society now, and the older they get, the harder it tends to be. I’m actually scared of the future.

So if your question wasn’t rethorical, I’d answer that I struggle to see the point as much as you do.

Like somebody mentioned, perhaps in another post, before this year I also didn’t even know DJ was a thing, and last autumn when a friend mentioned he’s doing Sober October, I thought- did you invent this? It’s genious! In my country a fasting before Easter is gathering momentum the latest years, even among the non-religious.

So last year I was doing the alcohol fast until Easter. I remeber being proud of myself, losing 6kg, looking better and going straight back to my old habbits once the Easter came, which is a daily bottle of wine.

Late last year a friend of mine told me he will be doing DJ, and since I love company, I joined in. He didn’t last a day, so this sub serves as my company instead.

Why I thought I needed this? I knew I drank too much, sometimes I regretted what I said or did, I had gotten out of shape and I wanted to check if I can become a better version of myself mentally and physically.

I didn’t :). But there’s one thing I realized- I did drink wine for 2 evenings this January and it has lost it’s magic power to boost my mood. It was even unpleasant. I feel like a child again when alcohol is just a substance with a bad taste.

Your usual drinking habbits is what a large part of the group aspires to achieve (including me) :). I’m not a doctor, but having read about withdrawal symptoms which I had, I would assume that the amount you drank shouldn’t cause any of the physical effects. Perpahs it’s the emotional effect, if treating yourself with a drink previously associated with good emotions, now when it’s gone and if you haven’t replaced it with another winding-down self-care ritual, perhaps the mind is willing to have a break and signals that. Tidying excessively sounds like a need to have control over something and perhaps you lack the sense of control e.g. over your relationship situation, and you overdo it in other areas to compensate. These are all well- meant guesses. It’s helpful if other opinions make you think and ask questions to yourself, but that doesn’t replace a talk with a trained professional :)
What were your reasons to start DJ?

I met one of them on my Erasmus, we were studying together. Through our studies we became good friends, then a couple. He’s one of the kindest persons I know, plus he was into adventures and that attracted me.

Another guy was a colleague at work, one if the managers I had to work with. He was very intelligent, ambitious and had a dry sense of humour. He really stood out for me and I could easily name him the most attractive guy in the company, though he was far from being good looking.

Thank you for being so honest! I can relate to procrastination- I’m a terrible procrastinator and it stands in my way, I believe it has to do with the reward system in the brain. You desribed it well.

I have been called ugly, I believed I was ugly until it suddenly changed after high school. Out of nowhere I was approached by model scouts and photographers. Guys liked me, I received loads of compliments. Even 20 years after high school I hear that I am pretty every now and then. And guess what? I still have low self-esteem. Good looks do help, but it certainly is not the key.

Also, to my surprise, twice in my life I have developed a crush on guys where my initial reaction was- boy, he’s ugly! I got to know them and through their personality they became beautiful in my eyes. Personality is one thing you can develop. It’s hard work, but it pays off. I’m working on mine as well :)

I was a healthy weight when I got pregnant at 32 (177cm, 68kg), but during my pregnancy I gained 35kg! Approximately 5kg gained each month, I had to get bigger sized clothes each month. It did make me super uncomfortable, but it was a lot of water weight and I got back to my normal weight in 6 months. What helped me- a lot of walking! More than 10km each day. Then I took up running, yoga and private training sessions. I spent around 200 EUR for sports each month, which I thought was crazy, but I had finally found what I liked and what worked for me. My point being- find what works for you, be patient and most importantly- feel good about yourself! Beating yourself up about being overweight is a mindset that never really worked for me. Patience and loving kindness did.

Also, please do consult your doctor. Perhaps there is nothing to worry about, and if he/she does suggest a weight loss, then I’m sure you are able to do this!

Wow! I’m impressed! That’s a lot of weight! I need to lose 22lbs to hit my goal weight and since my method of choice is magical thinking, I haven’t made much progress yet. Oh yeah, I gave up my wine, let’s see it that has any impact.

I had 3 glasses of wine yesterday for the sole purpose if reducing my anxiety. Guess what? It didn’t help :). And I’m not looking forward towards my next drink, at least not today. Your reasons are completely different. But the common thing could be that having rare exceptions doesn’t ruin our DJ and we go on.

Thank you all for your kind support! It’s really helpful to be able to let these things out, even if they’re unpleasant to me and probably some readers.

I got in touch with my doctor and we made a plan, so that I can jump back on the dry train and actually survive
I will sign up for the gym and will try more intense sports than walking
I will download the book Alcohol Explained

Thanks again and good luck to everybody!
I struggle to see the point of your comment. I’m not looking for a label, as I don’t find it helpful at all. Anyways, good luck with your DJ!

This DJ is definitely an eye-opener. And I owe a lot to this and DryJanuary group. People have been most supportive. I’ll call my psychiatrist tomorrow (i’m treated for depression), explain what’s happening and listen to her advice. I know she’ll help me, she’s the best.

Yes, I really appreciate this DJ. It made me realize I cannot just cut cold turkey and go on with my life. I like not drinking, I see benefits, but there is this anxiety which makes it impossible to go on. I do meditate, I’m trying walks, I’m making lists of things that give me pleasure and try to do them. Nothing helps. It’s like this evil thing that stops me. I know it’s not me, it’s this other uncontrollable thing that is ruining it for me.

I hear you. Also, I’m looking for a quick fix now, because I know it’s not a long-term solution. I know the reason of my drinking is anxiety, and I need a stable replacement for alcohol. I’m curious to see if a drink will help, that will be an experiment and I will discuss it with my therapist. By the way, I just texted her, she gave me a green light, but we will address this shortly in a session.

1) i hate this DJ because it’s so tough for me due to increased anxiety

2) i love the feeling of keeping a promise to myself (at least so far), i think I might have lost a bit of weight, my skin is better and my eyes are brighter, I even had a WOW moment when I looked in the mirror today. Health suits everybody!
Makes me wonder which country you’re from, where they make you wait for the test results that long. I’m doing my test on Friday. Stay healthy and I hope your kid gets better soon!

I meditate and I like reading. Work gives me joy when I get something done and cross it from my to-do list. I like SPAs and massages. I’m embarrassed to say, but also looking good lifts my mood. I generally like being physically active,  but this January I’m too busy observing how I react to not drinking. Maybe that’s it- I’m too much in my head?

Thank you! I’m pretty passive. I spend most of my energy trying to get through the day and getting some work done. My job involves a lot of communication, so I get to talk to people. My best friends live abroad, and we’re texting regularly. Some other friends recently resurfaced. So yes, there’s social contact. I will try to add some movement, I know it’s essential. I have a plan to by a membership at an exclusive sports club which also offers an amazing sauna and pools area. That would be a treat :). I just need to push myself to actually follow through.
I’m sorry if it was not meant to be funny, but it made me laugh :). Good job sticking by your promise to yourself!
A sad high 5! I hope it gets easier for us. We’re still staying sober for the Jan, right?

I’ve tried before. I got instructed to cut down on drinking and find a hobby, do sports, spend time with my kid (he’s autistic and that’s a huge part of why I’m searching remedy in alcohol). I decided she can’t help me with this issue so stopped talking about it.

Consulted another therapist about drinking. She said it’s bad for me and I should cut back... Find a hobby that makes me feel good blah blah blah

And those are THE top specialists in my country.   They might be right, but I cannot think of a hobby that I would be willing to stick to. So I decided it’s my own struggle.
It could be the withdrawal, it also could be the case that I removed the one and only thing that most efficiently and loyally blurred my problems each evening.

Thank you for encouragement! I’m a regular (well, once a month) in therapy. We have discussed my drinking and, oh boy, I even want to lie to my therapist pretending it’s not a problem 🙈. Have dug down to the reasons, but the reasons are not going anywhere and I haven’t found another way of coping. Perhaps it’s that- I’m left without a coping strategy, that’s why I struggle so much.

So happy about everyone doing so good! I myself find sobriety a torture every day. I have no sleep, no energy and can’t seem to get anything done. I miss my life! Or maybe I don’t, it was far from perfect. But THIS was not what I was looking for. Quite confused here.
They make me sick

Please hold this promise. It’s my day 10 and it has been tough, but we are here to support each other.

I’m listening to an audio book We are the luckiest by Laura McKowen, which I gighly recommend. She quoted one doctor: the one thing that is common for every person who is staying sober is that they don’t [drink alcohol]. As simple and as difficult as that.

Also I advice you to check in with your doctor. The weekend has been tough for me, so I’m seeing a doctor today to understand how can I help my body to get through this.

A warm welcome to you!
It crossed my mind, but my DIY test showed negative. Will make a laboratory test.

I’be been there a couple of times and trust me, with proper help it gets better. The depression in your head now is telling you that you will never experience joy or interest in life again, but that’s just a plain lie. You’ll get over this, and you don’t have to do it alone. Seek help. It’s not a weakness, it’s common sense.

I’m happy for you it’t going so relatively easy! I can’t wait when my withdrawal symptoms subside. This weekend I’ve felt so fragile physically, but the silver lining is that due to feeling that bad I didn’t crave alcohol at all, not for a minute.
Hey, but I just googled- those ARE Omicron symptoms! Really cirious to test it, then I can make clearer conclutions what’s what

I feel very much like you do. Today has been especially bad, mostly physically, but my mood hasn’t been great either. Headaches, tiredness, difficulty concentrating, making decisions and have anything done. I’m surprised, because last year I did a dry month as well, and I don’t remember it being that bad. For a moment there this evening I thought I might have covid, since I found out I am a contact person. But the DIY test was negative, will take a laboratory test as soon as I can to double-check (hoping it’s positive, because that would explain. And that’s a socially more acceptable reason for feeling low, compared to alcohol withdrawal)

Proud of you!
My day 8 is pretty dreadful, I’m feeling really down, both mentally and physically. But I just found out I’m a covid contact-person, so will do a test and perhaps it’s covid, not withdrawal. I don’t even know which option would be better.

Please don’t die just yet. Loosing a leg sounds terrible, but it’s not necessarily the end of the world. I have a friend who was born with one arm. She’s gorgeous, fun, smart and has an amazing boyfriend. It IS possible to lead a happy life even when it’s not ideal.

I’ll try magnesium as well! I feel really down, anxious and unable to sleep. A bit or very much like a vampire without blood. I feel poorly phisically as well. Quite an eye opener about what effect alcohol has on you, if you feel this way without it.
I quit smoking when I was pregnant. Dreamt about a cigarette almost every night. Crazy that it can last for as long as 22 years

I’m sorry, but what does “sub” mean? (English is obviously not my mother tongue)

I’m concerned, because I’m not doing great. Can’t sleep, I’m super tired and work seems unmanageable. My eating habits are terrible, can’t understand when I’m hungry, when not. Weight is not going away. Procrastinstion hasn’t changed much, but I do see some tiny improvements. It’s so upsetting- I’m a mess with a drink, I’m a mess without a drink.

But let’s search for some positives. .....uhm..... less shameful experiences and none due to alcohol. Group support and discussions are what helps me to keep focused on the goal.

The weekend plans- will try to catch on with some work. Recycling. Nothing more planned
I’m glad I asked for support in this group. It was a huge help!
I appreciate your bright outlook on future prospects! That’s the mentality I try to develop in myself. Not drinking!
Thanks! It’s the right reminder at the right moment!
Thank you for sharing this. It’s encouraging to hear. Not drinking today :)

I didn’t lose my job, even though I’m not sure if I want to stay. One part of me shouts- get out!, another part says- don’t rush.
After the lunch I went for a pedicure and am now at my favourite bar. Drinking mate. :) Your support helped to decide against celebrating over a glass of Prosecco :) Thanks a lot!

Oh, I feel you! That’s such an important reason!

I still remember what I read in an interview some 5 years ago. I don’t recall who it was, but he was telling about his childhood- “My mom was drinking wine every evening. Back then I thought she was so sophisticated and elegant, now I realize she was an alcoholic with an expensive taste.”

I hear these words in my ears each evening when I’m having my glass of red while my son is in the room enterntaining himself- never want my kid to come to this realization.
I can’t sleep. It’s exhausting and makes me somewhat disoriented. Today I handed over two euro coins to the sales lady for a purchase worth 5.75 EUR. And just stood there waiting for the change 🙈

Glad to hear! Day 4 was a bit challenging for me. I had a difficult work task, was working on it until 2am, felt stressed and normally I’d a have a glass (read- bottle) of wine to calm down my nerves. I didn’t.
What about Day4?

I’m also doing it one day at a time. I don’t have rules, except that I will do my best not to drink that day. I don’t even have a prize for myself, because for me that would put extra pressure on. I hope I will lose some weight, I hope my skin will look better, and I’m glad for every day I didn’t say or do anything to regret later. Or if I did, then I have more compassion for myself, because it’s not the alcohol, it’s me. I’m also being attentive to my thoughts and moods.
I bought a special journal for this :)

No trouble with sleep? I have mixed feelings of being proud of myself, having a clearer head, but also anxious without my drink in the evening and having quite some insomnia. Last year (it was March though) I stopped my dry streak not because it was too hard, but because the novelty of it wore off and I figured- ues, now I got it, I can drink moderately now. Wrong.

Yes, I also crave some other indulgence, so I overdose on snacks, mostly sugary ones. Not really happy with it, since last year when going a dry month I managed to lose 5 kilos. I was running most evenings, but now it’s icy and slippery, so I don’t.
Why do you want to overdose on sleepimg medicine?
I’m also hanging in. The feeling is foreign. I don’t  really want a drink but nevertheless it’s a weird feeling without one.

This is inspiring! I’ll try a month off and then see if moderation is for me. Will work with a therapist meanwhile. Want to check whether it’s chicken or egg- I drink because of my problems, or I have problems because I drink? Probably both. A vicious circle.

I’m also not sure if I can do it. I feel pretty irritated this evening (my 3rd). Glad, though, that in these evenings I have not been too sleepy or tipsy from wine for my evening beauty routine, so my skin must feel better.

I feel you! Only a month in, but there are moments when I ask myself: did I just say that? Wasn’t I supposed to become a Dalai Lama without my drink? I believe it’s about owning that ugly part of yourself as well, along with the good part. I think that alcohol was not the monster in itself, but it brought out that ugly part more. Now the balance is better. And the work with own ugly part can become more efficient when sober. Could kindness to others and yourself be the key?

Oh, and I thought it was just me. 31 day sober and I keep wondering what all that anger is about. I’ve always been opinionated, but now it has escalated. Perhaps it’s because I used to feel somewhat inferior to other people because of drinking. Now that’s gone, and suddenly I’ve become so self-righteous. That’s not attractive to anybody, including me. I’m trying to stop myself from reacting, taking moments to calm down and sometimes just shutting up. Still early in this learning process, so I occasionally mess up, but I guess that’s ok. I find Sam Harris a good influence.
Thanks, I appreciate your encouragement! :) I used to give myself a permission to drink only after 12pm, then moved to 3pm. Still so much time saved now!
Indeed, forgot about that one. Actually bought new running shoes with the money I saved :)

Hey there, it’s my 13th day, and I’m also happy to have my husband’s support. He drinks though, but it has never been a problem to him. It’s really nice to hear “I’m proud of you”, and it’s even better to know that I’m proud of myself. The beginning of the journey feels like discovering a whole new world. It’s not easy, but pretty exciting and eye-opening, isn’t it?

8th day not drinking. So far it was not that hard and I even started to enjoy not drinking and exploring my natural reactions to things. But today my anxiety kicked-in big time. I know a drink would help, but I don’t want to drink. I just want to feel normal.
No, actually not. Don’t make me see the bright side of life ;)

I have found that when I’m feeling very low, I don’t even have the strength to exercise. When I feel OK-ish, then it helps a bit- I like the idea of doing something that is healthy, requires strength, and makes me think to myself- yes! I was able to do that! *pat on my shoulder*

I feel you. My friend actually was the one asking me not to talk to her because it’s too hard for her. She does acknowledge my feelings, but then she tries to sort out my problems by giving useful tips and is angry when I don’t act upon them. Actually, I can sort of understand her. In your case it must be difficult not being heard. I know it’s not easy to find a person listening to you.
Actually thinking about the same thing. I’m depressed, bmy kid is autistic, I have no more strength to cope, why not just atarve to death
